result.title: From Forecasting to World Modeling: Can Temporal Foundation Models Recover Causal Response?
result.comment: Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Foundation Models for Temporal Systems (FMTS), non-archival. 15 pages, 2 figures, 3 tables
result.summary: A model that forecasts sales accurately can still mislead a retailer about how sales respond to a price change. We evaluate released tabular and time-series foundation models, as well as a foundation model pretrained specifically to estimate causal effects. We report three findings. First, forecast accuracy does not indicate the accuracy of the predicted effect of price, both on simulated data in which the true effect is known and on real retail sales records. Second, for the tabular foundation models, additional context improves forecasts but not the predicted effect of price. Third, instrumental variables, the standard remedy in econometrics, reduce this error only when supplied in a specific form and increase it for every model under confounding when supplied as raw instruments.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在已知真实效应的模拟数据与真实零售销售记录上评测表格与时间序列基础模型，考察其预测的「价格效应」是否准确，发现预测精度不能指示因果效应精度、增加上下文只改善预测、工具变量仅在特定形式下有效。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「预测准 ≠ 恢复正确的因果响应」这一诊断思路，可能为 LVR 中判断答案是否真正利用 latent 内容、以及贡献分配与评价设计提供参照，但属时间序列因果效应估计，迁移需较多核查。
